cloudflare_aaa_id_response: A webhook destination for Cloudflare's Notifications service. Defines the URL Cloudflare posts a notification payload to when a configured alert fires, with an optional shared secret sent in the `cf-webhook-auth` header so the receiving endpoint can verify the request originated from Cloudflare.
cloudflare_aaa_schemas_single_response: A webhook destination for Cloudflare's Notifications service, the same real concept as cloudflare_aaa_id_response discovered via a distinct read path in Cloudflare's own spec. Defines the URL and optional shared secret used to deliver notification payloads.
cloudflare_aaa_single_response: A notification policy in Cloudflare's Notifications (Alerting) service. Defines which event type triggers a notification (`alert_type`), any filters narrowing which events qualify, and the delivery mechanisms (e.g. email addresses, webhook destination IDs) notifications are dispatched to.
cloudflare_access_idp_federation_grant_r: Grants federation to an existing Cloudflare Access identity provider (`idp_id`), the mechanism by which an already-configured identity provider is included in Access's federated authentication flow.
cloudflare_access_policy_update_resp: Represents a test run of one or more Access policies against a simulated request. Used to check whether specific Access policies would allow or deny a given request without applying them for real.
cloudflare_access_single_response_10: An account-level Access policy. Defines the authentication and authorization rules (approval requirements, MFA configuration, browser isolation, session duration) applied to requests for the applications this policy is attached to.
cloudflare_access_single_response_11: A custom page for Cloudflare Access -- branded HTML shown to end users during the Access authentication flow (e.g. a custom login or blocked-access page), identified by its own `type` and referenceable by the applications it's assigned to.
cloudflare_access_single_response_14: An Access tag -- a label that can be attached to Access applications, used to group and filter applications in the Cloudflare dashboard and API.
cloudflare_access_single_response_17: A zone-level Access group. Defines a reusable set of Include/Exclude/Require authentication rules (matched against a user's identity, IP, device posture, etc.) that Access policies can reference by group instead of repeating the same rules.
cloudflare_access_single_response_18: A zone-level Access service token -- a non-interactive credential (client ID/secret pair) that lets a service authenticate to an Access-protected application without a human login. Supports secret rotation via `client_secret_version`, keeping the previous secret valid until `previous_client_secret_expires_at`.
cloudflare_access_single_response_2: An account-level Access service token, the same real concept as cloudflare_access_single_response_18 scoped to an account rather than a single zone -- a non-interactive credential letting a service authenticate to Access-protected applications, with rotation support via `client_secret_version`.
cloudflare_access_single_response_20: A zone-level Access mutual TLS (mTLS) certificate, used to authenticate client devices to Access-protected applications on the hostnames listed in `associated_hostnames`.
cloudflare_access_single_response_22: An Access policy scoped to a specific zone-level Access application. Defines the Include/Exclude/Require rules and the resulting `decision` (allow/deny/bypass) applied when a request matches, with `precedence` controlling evaluation order among the application's own policies.
cloudflare_access_single_response_4: An account-level Access group, the same real concept as cloudflare_access_single_response_17 scoped to an account rather than a single zone -- a reusable set of Include/Exclude/Require rules Access policies can reference by group.
cloudflare_access_single_response_6: An account-level Access mutual TLS (mTLS) certificate, the same real concept as cloudflare_access_single_response_20 scoped to an account rather than a single zone.
cloudflare_access_single_user_response: An Access user record for the account -- represents an individual who has authenticated through Access, identified by their email address.
cloudflare_addressing_full_response: An Address Map in Cloudflare's BYOIP (Bring Your Own IP) addressing service. Groups a set of IP addresses (`ips`) and assigns them to specific zones or the whole account (`memberships`) so Cloudflare's DNS responds with those IPs only for the assigned scope, once `enabled`.
cloudflare_addressing_single_response: An IP address prefix (BYOIP) registered with Cloudflare for advertisement under a given Autonomous System Number (`asn`). `loa_document_id` references the uploaded Letter of Authorization proving the account's right to advertise the prefix; `delegate_loa_creation` lets Cloudflare generate that document on the owner's behalf instead.
cloudflare_addressing_single_response_bg: A BGP-advertised sub-prefix of a parent BYOIP address prefix, identified by its own CIDR block. Represents a smaller range Cloudflare announces via BGP within the bounds of the parent prefix.
cloudflare_alexandria_get_application_re: An application entry in Cloudflare's Resource Library -- a catalogued real-world application identified by the hostnames, IP subnets, and port/protocol pairs its traffic matches, referenced elsewhere in Cloudflare's platform (e.g. traffic policies) by name instead of its raw network signature.
cloudflare_api_shield_public_schema_succ: An API schema registered with API Shield's schema validation feature. `source` holds the raw OpenAPI schema (JSON or YAML); once `validation_enabled`, Cloudflare validates incoming requests against it.
cloudflare_api_shield_single_operation_r: An API operation tracked by API Shield -- a specific HTTP method and endpoint template (path parameters represented as `{varN}` placeholders) on a given host, the unit API Shield's discovery, schema validation, and rate limiting features operate on.
cloudflare_app: An application registered in Cloudflare's Flagship feature-flag/experimentation platform, identified by `name`. Serves as the parent container for that application's own flags and variations.
cloudflare_asset: An asset attached to a Cloudforce One threat intelligence request -- a supporting file or artifact associated with a specific request in Cloudforce One's workflow.
cloudflare_bill_subs_api_account_subscri: An account-level billing subscription -- the paid plan or add-on component Cloudflare bills the account for, with `rate_plan` naming the plan, `component_values` any usage-based configuration, and `current_period_start`/`current_period_end` the active billing cycle.
cloudflare_bill_subs_api_payment_method_: A payment method on file for the account's billing. Cloudflare's payment-methods API supports both card and bank-transfer-style payment methods, with the bank-specific fields (routing number, account type, country) populated only for bank-based methods.
cloudflare_binding: A binding between a BYOIP address prefix (or a CIDR range within it) and a Cloudflare network service (`service_id`), directing traffic to that prefix through the bound service.
cloudflare_brand_protection_api_error: The error response shape for Brand Protection's internal submission endpoint. Discovered as a resource because the endpoint's own create and read operations share this shape; low confidence this represents a real, durable domain entity rather than an error envelope -- worth a second look against Cloudflare's own current API reference before treating as authoritative.
cloudflare_bucket: An R2 object storage bucket. `location_hint` optionally requests that new objects be stored close to a given region; `storage_class` sets the default storage class (e.g. Standard or Infrequent Access) for newly uploaded objects.
cloudflare_bulk: A bulk remediation job in Email Security's investigation tooling -- applies a single action (e.g. move, delete) across every message matching `search_params`, recording the expected disposition and an optional comment for audit purposes.
cloudflare_calls_app_response_single: A Cloudflare Calls application -- the top-level container for a WebRTC application's own SFU/TURN usage, identified by an internal `name` not shown to end users.
cloudflare_calls_turn_key_response_singl: A TURN key for Cloudflare Calls -- credentials used to authenticate to Cloudflare's TURN relay service for WebRTC NAT traversal, identified by an internal `name` not shown to end users.
cloudflare_category: A threat event category in Cloudforce One's threat intelligence platform. Classifies events against real-world threat frameworks (`mitre_attack`, `mitre_capec`) and cyber kill chain stage (`kill_chain`).
cloudflare_client_side_security_get_zone: A Page Shield policy -- defines an action Cloudflare takes against client-side scripts/connections matching a Firewall-rule-syntax `expression` on the zone, part of Page Shield's client-side security (Magecart/supply-chain attack) protection.
cloudflare_cloudforce_one_rule_preview: A structured detection rule in Cloudforce One's threat intelligence platform. `condition` holds nested match logic (up to 10 levels deep) and `content` the rule body itself; `is_public` controls whether other internal accounts can see the rule.
cloudflare_collection: A collection in Cloudforce One's threat intelligence platform -- a saved grouping of related threat intelligence items (e.g. indicators, events) for organization and sharing. Low confidence: the underlying schema carries no named fields beyond the generic response envelope, so this reading is inferred from the endpoint's own path, not from field content.
cloudflare_commit: A repository in Cloudflare's Artifacts (container registry) service, despite its own generated name -- `default_branch`, `read_only`, and `name` describe a repository, not a commit. This is a real noun-derivation mismatch in the generated type name, not a docs gap; flagged for a rename pass rather than corrected here, since this session's own scope is create-binding correctness, not noun quality.
cloudflare_config: A Hyperdrive configuration -- Cloudflare's connection-pooling and caching layer in front of an external database. `origin` defines the real database Hyperdrive connects to, `mtls` optional origin authentication, `caching` its own query-caching behavior, and `origin_connection_limit` the pool's own soft cap on origin connections.
cloudflare_cost: A custom AI provider registered with AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the real fields (`base_url`, `curl_example`, `js_example`, `headers`) describe a self-hosted or third-party LLM provider registration, not a cost record. A real noun-derivation mismatch (this endpoint's response schema is shared with several other generated names -- see cloudflare_custom_domain, cloudflare_custom_provider -- all really the same AI Gateway/custom-provider concept), not a docs gap.
cloudflare_crawl: A crawl job in Browser Rendering -- triggers Cloudflare's managed headless-browser service to crawl one or more pages, returning the job's own real result once complete.
cloudflare_credential: A single credential within a Vulnerability Scanner credential set -- an authentication value (e.g. API key, session token) attached to outgoing scan requests via a named header or cookie (`location`, `location_name`). `value` is write-only and never returned in API responses.
cloudflare_credential_set: A credential set in Vulnerability Scanner -- a named group of authentication credentials the scanner attaches to its own requests when authenticated scanning is needed, containing one or more individual credentials.
cloudflare_custom: A custom Data Loss Prevention (DLP) profile -- defines the detection entries, associated data classes/tags, and match-sensitivity settings (`confidence_threshold`, `allowed_match_count`, OCR/context-awareness toggles) DLP policies evaluate content against.
cloudflare_custom_domain: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- Cloudflare's proxy and observability layer in front of one or more LLM providers. Configures caching (`cache_ttl`, `cache_invalidate_on_update`), authentication requirements, and logging/log-push behavior (`collect_logs`, `logpush`, `log_management`) for requests routed through the gateway. A real noun-derivation mismatch shared with several other generated names -- see cloudflare_cost, cloudflare_custom_provider.
cloudflare_custom_indicator_feeds_indica: A custom threat intelligence indicator feed registered with Cloudflare's Threat Intelligence (Intel) service -- a named, described source of indicators the account can upload and query alongside Cloudflare's own built-in feeds.
cloudflare_custom_pages_custom_asset_res: An asset (e.g. an image) used by a custom page -- referenced by name and fetched from `url`, used to brand Cloudflare's own served custom error/challenge pages.
cloudflare_custom_pages_custom_page_resu: A custom page -- Cloudflare-served HTML (e.g. a branded error or challenge page) hosted at `url`, with `state` controlling whether the custom version is active or Cloudflare's own default page is served instead.
cloudflare_custom_prompt_topic: A custom prompt topic for DLP's AI-prompt inspection -- defines a named topic (`topic`) the DLP profile `profile_id` scans AI prompts/content for, alongside Cloudflare's own built-in topics.
cloudflare_custom_provider: A custom AI provider registered with AI Gateway, the same real concept as cloudflare_cost discovered via a distinct read path in Cloudflare's own spec -- lets AI Gateway route requests to a self-hosted or third-party LLM endpoint.
cloudflare_data_class: A DLP data class -- a named detection definition (`expression`) DLP profiles reference to identify a specific category of sensitive data, with `sensitivity_levels` and associated `data_tags` used for classification and reporting.
cloudflare_data_tag: A DLP data tag within a data tag category -- a named label DLP profiles attach to matched content for classification and reporting, grouped under its parent category.
cloudflare_data_tag_category: A DLP data tag category -- a named grouping for data tags, optionally seeded from a built-in `template_id` instead of an explicit tag list.
cloudflare_database: A D1 database -- Cloudflare's managed serverless SQL database. `jurisdiction` restricts where the database runs and stores data; `primary_location_hint` requests a specific region for the primary instance; `read_replication` configures read replicas.
cloudflare_dataset: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway, cloudflare_cost, cloudflare_custom_domain, and cloudflare_custom_provider, all discovered from response schemas sharing the identical AI Gateway shape under different generated names. A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_deploy_hook: A deploy hook for a Cloudflare Workers Builds pipeline -- a webhook-triggered mechanism that starts a new deployment of the named branch when called, identified by its own UUID.
cloudflare_deployment: A Cloudflare Pages deployment. Built either from a git branch (`branch`, with commit metadata) or from directly uploaded files/Worker bundle (`_worker_js`/`_worker_bundle`, mutually exclusive), with `_headers`/`_redirects`/`_routes_json` as Pages' own build-time configuration files.
cloudflare_deployment_group: A deployment group for Cloudflare's Device (WARP client) management -- groups devices under a shared `version_config` and set of `policy_ids`, used to roll out WARP client versions and device policies to a defined subset of devices.
cloudflare_digital_experience_monitoring: A Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) test -- configures the WARP client to periodically run a synthetic test (`data` holds the test's own configuration) against `target_policies`, on a recurring `interval`, for monitoring end-user network/application experience.
cloudflare_dls_prefix_binding_response: A binding between a BYOIP prefix's CIDR range and a managed region (`region_key`) in Cloudflare's Data Localization Suite -- restricts where traffic for that CIDR is processed.
cloudflare_document_fingerprint: A document fingerprint for DLP -- a hash-based detector that flags content matching a specific, previously fingerprinted document above `match_percent` similarity, rather than a pattern-based rule.
cloudflare_domain: A protected domain in Email Security's settings. Configures inbound/outbound TLS requirements, IP restrictions, and delivery/disposition handling for mail on this domain.
cloudflare_dos_dns_protection_rule_respo: A DNS Protection rule under Magic Transit's Advanced DNS Protection. Sets detection sensitivity (`burst_sensitivity`, `profile_sensitivity`, `rate_sensitivity`) and `mode` (enabled/disabled/monitoring) for a given `scope` (global, region, or datacenter), including whether to block DNS ANY queries.
cloudflare_dos_expression_filter_respons: A SYN Protection filter under Magic Transit's Advanced TCP Protection. Uses a Firewall-rule-syntax `expression` to scope which traffic the surrounding SYN Protection rules apply to, with its own independent `mode`.
cloudflare_dos_infra_prefix_response: An allowlisted prefix under Magic Transit's Advanced TCP Protection -- a CIDR range exempted from TCP-protection mitigation once `enabled`.
cloudflare_dos_prefix_response: A prefix under Magic Transit's Advanced TCP Protection -- a CIDR range that can be `excluded` from protection, distinct from cloudflare_dos_infra_prefix_response's own allowlist mechanism.
cloudflare_dos_syn_protection_rule_respo: A SYN Protection rule under Magic Transit's Advanced TCP Protection. Sets detection sensitivity, `mode`, and `mitigation_type` (challenge or retransmit) for SYN-flood mitigation at a given `scope`.
cloudflare_dos_tcp_flow_protection_rule_: A TCP Flow Protection rule under Magic Transit's Advanced TCP Protection. Sets detection sensitivity and `mode` for anomalous-TCP-flow mitigation at a given `scope`.
cloudflare_email_destination_address_res: A verified destination email address for Email Routing -- an external mailbox routing rules can forward zone email to, once the address owner confirms a verification email.
cloudflare_email_rule_response_single: An Email Routing rule for a zone. `matchers` define which incoming addresses the rule applies to and `actions` where matching mail is forwarded; `source` distinguishes rules managed via the dashboard/API/Terraform from ones managed by a Worker's own wrangler configuration.
cloudflare_email_sending_subdomain_respo: A subdomain configured for outbound Email Sending on a zone -- enables sending authenticated mail from the given subdomain (or, with the account-level wildcard feature enabled, a wildcard subdomain).
cloudflare_entry: A DLP detection entry -- a single pattern-based rule (`pattern`) attached to a DLP profile (`profile_id`), the individual detector a custom DLP profile's own `entries` list is built from.
cloudflare_evaluation: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway and its sibling generated names (see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list). A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_event: A threat event in Cloudforce One's threat intelligence platform -- a recorded observation (attacker, target, category, indicator) within a dataset, the core unit Cloudforce One's own categories, rules, and collections organize and reference.
cloudflare_finetune_asset: A fine-tune asset for Workers AI -- a file (e.g. training data) associated with a fine-tuned model (`finetune_id`), identified within that fine-tune by `file_name`.
cloudflare_firewall_filter_response_sing: A zone-level (legacy) Firewall filter -- a reusable Firewall-rule-syntax `expression`, referenced by one or more firewall rules rather than repeating the expression inline. Superseded in newer Cloudflare accounts by the Ruleset Engine, but still live for zones on the legacy Firewall Rules product.
cloudflare_firewall_filter_rules_single_: A zone-level (legacy) Firewall rule -- pairs a `filter` (a Firewall-rule-syntax expression) with an `action` to take when matched traffic exceeds a configured threshold.
cloudflare_firewall_firewalluablock_resp: A zone-level User Agent Blocking rule (legacy Firewall product) -- blocks or challenges requests whose User-Agent header matches `configuration`, with `mode` set to a not-yet-migrated legacy shape distinct from the newer Ruleset Engine equivalent.
cloudflare_firewall_override_response_si: A zone-level WAF override (legacy Firewall product) -- adjusts the WAF's own rule behavior for requests matching the given `urls`, predating the Ruleset Engine's own per-request override mechanism.
cloudflare_firewall_ratelimit_response_s: A zone-level rate limiting rule (legacy Firewall product). Counts traffic matching `match` over a rolling `period`, applying `action` once `threshold` is exceeded within that window.
cloudflare_firewall_response_single: An account-level IP Access Rule -- allows, blocks, or challenges requests from a matched IP/IP range/country/ASN (`configuration`) across every zone on the account, with `mode` setting the action taken.
cloudflare_firewall_rule_single_response: A user-level IP Access Rule -- the same real concept as cloudflare_firewall_response_single, scoped to the authenticated user's own account context (`/user/...`) rather than an explicit account ID.
cloudflare_firewall_zonelockdown_respons: A zone-level Zone Lockdown rule (legacy Firewall product) -- restricts access to the URLs listed in `urls` so only the IP addresses/CIDR ranges in `configurations` may reach them, evaluated in `priority` order relative to other lockdown rules.
cloudflare_flag: A feature flag within a Flagship application. `default_variation` is served when the flag is off or no `rules` match; `rules` are evaluated in ascending priority order to select a different variation for matching requests.
cloudflare_gateway: An AI Gateway -- Cloudflare's proxy and observability layer in front of one or more LLM providers. Configures caching (`cache_ttl`, `cache_invalidate_on_update`), authentication requirements, and logging/log-push behavior (`collect_logs`, `logpush`, `log_management`) for requests routed through the gateway. The one correctly-named wire among a real cluster of generated-name mismatches sharing this same response shape -- see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list.
cloudflare_group: A group within a Cloudforce One threat intelligence dataset -- a named collection of `members` (other dataset entities) for organizing related threat intelligence data.
cloudflare_healthchecks_single_response: A zone-level health check. Periodically probes `address` (an origin hostname or IP) from `check_regions`, tracking consecutive failures/successes against configurable thresholds before flipping the origin's own reported health status.
cloudflare_hold: A zone hold -- when set, blocks any zone activation for the hostname (e.g. via a plan change or ownership transfer) until explicitly released or, if `hold_after` is set, until that time passes. `include_subdomains` extends the same restriction to subdomains.
cloudflare_iam_response_single_account: A Cloudflare account -- the top-level billing and organizational container every zone, user, and resource belongs to. `unit` optionally places the new account under a tenant unit for multi-account (Tenant) management.
cloudflare_iam_scim_group: A SCIM Group for account-level user provisioning -- represents a group of users as defined by an external identity provider, kept in sync via the SCIM protocol; system groups (Cloudflare-managed) are distinguished from custom groups by ID prefix.
cloudflare_iam_scim_user: A SCIM User for account-level user provisioning -- represents an individual user as defined by an external identity provider (IdP), kept in sync via the SCIM protocol. `user_name` (the user's email) is the real, unique identifier; `external_id` lets the IdP track its own mapping.
cloudflare_iam_single_membership_respons: An account membership -- represents a user's own invited-or-active membership in an account. Its own real, narrow write surface is accepting or rejecting a pending invitation (`status`), not full membership management.
cloudflare_iam_sso_connector_response: An SSO connector for account-level authentication -- links a verified `email_domain` to an SSO identity provider, so users signing in with that email domain authenticate via SSO instead of a Cloudflare password. `begin_verification` starts the domain-ownership verification flow.
cloudflare_image: A Cloudflare Images image (the v1 API). Uploaded either as a direct file, from a source `url`, or referenced later via `id`; `metadata` is an arbitrary user-defined key-value store for linking the image back to an external system of record.
cloudflare_images_image_response_single: A Cloudflare Images image -- the same real concept as cloudflare_image, discovered via the images/v1 path family rather than the v1/images family (Cloudflare's own spec carries both as parallel, real API generations for the same product).
cloudflare_images_image_variant_simple_r: A Cloudflare Images variant -- a named, reusable image-resizing configuration (`options`) other parts of the platform reference by `id` (or via `variant_id`) instead of repeating resize parameters per request.
cloudflare_images_sourcingkit_migration_: A Sourcing Kit migration for Cloudflare Images -- a one-time bulk import job that copies objects from an existing external source (`source_id`, e.g. an S3-compatible bucket) into Cloudflare Images, with `conflict_behaviour`/`path_prefix`/`root_directory` controlling how the import is scoped and reconciled.
cloudflare_images_sourcingkit_source_sin: A Sourcing Kit source for Cloudflare Images -- registers an external storage bucket (`vendor`, `bucket`, `secret` credentials) as a source Sourcing Kit migrations can import from.
cloudflare_index: A Vectorize index -- Cloudflare's managed vector database. `config` defines the index's own vector dimensionality/metric; the index is the unit Workers bindings query for vector similarity search.
cloudflare_instance: An AI Search instance (formerly AutoRAG) -- Cloudflare's managed retrieval-augmented-generation pipeline. Configures the embedding model, chunking strategy (`chunk_size`, `chunk_overlap`), response caching (`cache_ttl`, `cache_threshold`), and which AI Gateway (`ai_gateway_id`) and model requests are routed through.
cloudflare_integration: A Zero Trust Risk Scoring integration -- connects an external identity/risk signal source (e.g. an Okta tenant, `tenant_url`) so its own risk signals feed into Cloudflare's device/user risk scoring.
cloudflare_intel_sinkholes_ingress_singl: An ingress rule for a Threat Intelligence sinkhole -- a BYOIP CIDR block (owned by the account) that routes matching traffic into the parent sinkhole for capture and analysis.
cloudflare_intel_sinkholes_sinkhole_sing: A Threat Intelligence sinkhole -- a managed collection endpoint for redirected malicious/suspicious traffic. Optionally stores large captured request bodies in an account-owned R2 bucket (`r2_bucket`/`r2_id`/`r2_secret`).
cloudflare_ip_profile: A Device IP profile for Zero Trust device management -- matches devices via a wirefilter `match` expression (e.g. by identity or group) and applies IP-related settings from the bound `subnet_id`, evaluated across profiles in ascending `precedence` order.
cloudflare_item: An AI Search namespace, despite its own generated name -- an isolated document collection within AI Search that a given instance searches over, distinct from cloudflare_instance itself. A real noun-derivation mismatch (the endpoint is ai-search/namespaces, not a generic 'item'), not a docs gap.
cloudflare_job: An AI Search instance, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_instance, discovered via a distinct read path in Cloudflare's own spec. A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_letter: A takedown notice letter in Cloudforce One's Brand Protection service -- a generated legal notice document (`letter_text`, from `template_id`) attached to a specific takedown notice, tracking its own `letter_type`.
cloudflare_level: A sensitivity level within a DLP sensitivity group -- a named tier (e.g. low/medium/high) DLP profiles reference to weight how strongly a match should be treated.
cloudflare_lex_dataset_detail_response: A dataset registered with Logpush's Log Explorer. `dataset` names the real Cloudflare log dataset to ingest (e.g. `http_requests`); `fields`/`filter` narrow which fields and events are ingested, defaulting to everything when omitted.
cloudflare_lists_list_response_collectio: A zone/account-level list (Cloudflare's Lists product) -- a named, typed collection (`kind`: IP addresses, ASNs, hostnames, or redirects) referenced by expression in Firewall/Ruleset rules instead of enumerating values inline.
cloudflare_load_balancing_monitor_group_: A Load Balancing monitor group -- groups several individual health-check monitors (`members`) so a load balancer pool can reference the group instead of a single monitor, treating pool health as the aggregate of the group's own monitors.
cloudflare_load_balancing_schemas_single: A Load Balancing origin pool, scoped to the authenticated user rather than an account (`/user/...`). Groups origins behind shared health-check settings (`monitor`, `check_regions`, `minimum_origins`) and geographic metadata used for proximity-based steering.
cloudflare_log: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway and its sibling generated names (see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list). A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_logpush_logpush_job_response_: A Logpush job -- continuously exports a named `dataset` (e.g. HTTP requests, firewall events) to an external `destination_conf` (e.g. an S3 bucket), with `filter` narrowing which events are included and `max_upload_*` fields controlling batch size and cadence.
cloudflare_logpush_transformer_response_: A Logpush transformer -- a named SQL query (`code`, up to 32KB) that reshapes a Logpush dataset before export, referenced by Logpush jobs instead of exporting the dataset's own raw shape.
cloudflare_magic_acl_single_response: An Access Control List (ACL) rule for a Magic WAN site. Controls traffic forwarding between two LANs (`lan_1`/`lan_2`) at the site, including whether matched traffic is forwarded locally or sent to Cloudflare, and whether the rule applies in one direction or both.
cloudflare_magic_lan_single_response: A LAN interface on a Magic WAN site. Configures VLAN tagging, static or DHCP addressing, routed subnets reachable through the interface, and its role in the site's own HA/breakout/prioritized-traffic configuration.
cloudflare_magic_magic_bgp_filter_profil: A BGP filter profile for Magic WAN -- a named, reusable set of CIDR prefix match targets and the `match_action` (e.g. permit/deny) to take on routes matching them, applied to BGP peering sessions.
cloudflare_magic_redundancy_group_with_m: A redundancy group for Magic WAN -- groups two or more GRE/IPsec tunnels (`members`) so traffic automatically fails over between them if one tunnel goes down.
cloudflare_magic_route_single_response: A static route for Magic WAN. Directs traffic matching `prefix` to `nexthop`, with `priority`/`weight`/`scope` controlling selection among multiple matching routes (including ECMP).
cloudflare_magic_site_single_response: A Magic WAN site -- a physical or virtual location connected via one or two Magic Connectors (`connector_id`, `secondary_connector_id` for high availability), identified by geographic `location`.
cloudflare_magic_transit_endpoint_health: An endpoint health check for Magic Transit diagnostics -- periodically probes a given `endpoint` IP using `check_type`, independent of the Load Balancing product's own health checks.
cloudflare_magic_tunnel_single_response: A GRE tunnel for Magic Transit/Magic WAN. Defines both tunnel endpoints (`cloudflare_gre_endpoint`, `customer_gre_endpoint`), the point-to-point interface addressing, MTU, and optional BGP/health-check configuration for the tunnel.
cloudflare_magic_visibility_mnm_mnm_rule: A Magic Network Monitoring (MNM) rule -- alerts when traffic matching the rule's own `prefixes` exceeds a `bandwidth_threshold`/`packet_threshold` (or a statistical z-score threshold) for a sustained `duration`, optionally auto-advertising the affected prefixes via Magic Transit as a mitigation.
cloudflare_magic_wan_single_response: A WAN-facing interface on a Magic WAN site, the site's own external/internet-facing counterpart to a LAN interface. Configures VLAN tagging, static or DHCP addressing, and interface priority for outbound routing.
cloudflare_mcn_get_onramp_response: A Magic Cloud Networking (MCN) onramp -- attaches a public cloud provider's own network (`cloud_type`, `cloud_asn`) to Magic WAN, with `attached_hubs`/`attached_vpcs` listing what it connects and `dynamic_routing` enabling BGP-based route exchange with the cloud side.
cloudflare_mcn_read_account_catalog_sync: A catalog sync for Magic Cloud Networking -- continuously syncs resource metadata (`policy` controls which resources) from a cloud provider into Cloudflare's own resource catalog for that MCN account.
cloudflare_mcn_read_account_provider_res: A cloud provider registration for Magic Cloud Networking -- represents a connected public cloud account/subscription (`cloud_type`, `friendly_name`) MCN onramps and catalog syncs are scoped to.
cloudflare_meeting: A RealtimeKit meeting -- a scheduled or ad-hoc video/audio session. Configures recording (`record_on_start`, `recording_config`), transcription and AI-generated summaries (`ai_config`, `transcribe_on_end`, `summarize_on_end`), and live-streaming behavior for the session.
cloudflare_memory: An Agent Memory namespace -- an isolated storage space for an AI agent's own persistent memory records, identified by `namespace_name` (optionally scoped to a `profile_name`). The same real endpoint and shape as cloudflare_namespace, discovered via a distinct read path in Cloudflare's own spec.
cloudflare_namespace: An Agent Memory namespace -- an isolated storage space for an AI agent's own persistent memory records. The same real entity as cloudflare_memory, discovered via a distinct read path in Cloudflare's own spec.
cloudflare_nsc_cni: A Cloud Network Interconnect (CNI) -- a point-to-point link between Cloudflare's network and a customer's own network, configured with BGP (`bgp`, `bgp_mode` controlling the customer-facing routing mode) and the IP addressing (`cust_ip`, `p2p_ip`) for each end of the link.
cloudflare_observatory_page_test_respons: A Speed/Observatory page test -- triggers a synthetic performance test of `url` from a given `region`, the mechanism behind Cloudflare's own Observatory page-speed reports.
cloudflare_one_integration_detail_respon: A Zero Trust (Cloudflare One) SaaS integration -- connects a third-party application (`application`, e.g. Google Workspace, AWS) via `auth_method` and `credentials`, with `dlp_profiles` and `permissions` scoping what DLP/CASB visibility and control Cloudflare gets into that application.
cloudflare_organization: A Cloudflare Organization -- a real, distinct multi-account management concept (Tenant's own top-level grouping) above individual accounts, with an optional `parent` organization and its own `profile`/`meta` for organization-level settings.
cloudflare_origin_cloud_region: An origin cloud region mapping for zone caching -- associates an origin IP address with the specific cloud vendor region it's hosted in, letting Cloudflare route or cache traffic with awareness of the origin's own real cloud placement.
cloudflare_pagerule: A (legacy) Page Rule for a zone. Matches requests against `targets` (URL patterns) and either redirects them or overrides zone settings (but not both) via `actions`, evaluated in `priority` order. Superseded for new configuration by the Ruleset Engine's own dynamic redirects and settings overrides, but still live for zones using the legacy product.
cloudflare_participant: A participant added to a RealtimeKit meeting -- represents one attendee, identified by a caller-supplied `custom_participant_id`, with `preset_name` applying a pre-configured role/permission set to that participant.
cloudflare_pipeline: A Cloudflare Pipeline -- a managed streaming ETL pipeline that processes ingested events through a `sql` transformation before writing them to a destination (e.g. an R2 bucket).
cloudflare_policy: A remediation policy in Data Security Posture Management (DSPM). Defines `actions` to take automatically when a specific `finding_type_id` is triggered, scoped to either all integrations or an explicit `integration_ids` list.
cloudflare_portal: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) portal in Access's AI Controls. Exposes one or more registered MCP `servers` at a given `hostname`, with `code_mode` controlling whether connecting clients may use Code Mode and `secure_web_gateway` optionally routing outbound MCP traffic through Zero Trust.
cloudflare_posture_api_export_job_respon: A content export job in Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) -- exports flagged content matching the given filters (DLP profile, integration, affliction date range, search term) for offline review.
cloudflare_posture_api_finding_instance_: An archive action on one or more DSPM finding instances -- marks the listed `check_instances` as archived, removing them from active review without deleting the underlying finding.
cloudflare_posture_api_finding_response: An ignore action on one or more DSPM findings -- marks the listed `checks` as ignored, suppressing them from active review.
cloudflare_posture_api_webhook_response: A webhook configuration for Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) -- sends DSPM findings/events to `destination_url`, with `authentication_type`/`signing_secret` configuring how the receiving endpoint verifies the request and `headers` adding custom request headers.
cloudflare_preset: A participant preset for RealtimeKit -- a named, reusable role/permission/UI configuration (`config`, `permissions`, `ui`) meetings assign to participants by `preset_name` instead of configuring each participant individually.
cloudflare_priority: Represents a query for prioritized Cloudforce One requests -- a paginated listing of requests, filtered/sorted by priority rather than a standalone priority entity in its own right.
cloudflare_project: A Cloudflare Pages project. Defines the connected source control repository (`source`), `build_config` for how to build it, `production_branch`, and per-environment `deployment_configs`.
cloudflare_query: A saved query in Cloudforce One's threat intelligence platform. Stores `query_json` (the query parameters) under a unique `name`, with optional alerting (`alert_enabled`, `alert_rollup_enabled`) and WAF-rule-list integration (`rule_enabled`, `rule_list_id`) for automatically blocking on matches.
cloudflare_queue: A Cloudflare Queue -- a managed message queue Workers can produce to and consume from, identified by `queue_name`.
cloudflare_realtimekit_webhook_success_r: A webhook for RealtimeKit -- sends selected meeting `events` to `url` when `enabled`, the mechanism by which an application is notified of real-time meeting activity outside the SDK's own client-side callbacks.
cloudflare_recording: A recording of a RealtimeKit meeting (`meeting_id`). Configures audio/interactive recording settings, an optional custom `url` to record an arbitrary screen instead of the meeting itself, storage destination (`storage_config`, `realtimekit_bucket_config`), and whether multiple concurrent recordings are allowed for the same meeting.
cloudflare_regional_hostname: A regional hostname -- restricts where a given zone subdomain's traffic is processed (`region_key`) and how it's routed (`routing`), part of Cloudflare's Data Localization Suite.
cloudflare_registrar_api_registration_re: A domain registration through Cloudflare Registrar. Registers `domain_name` for a term of `years`, with `contacts`/`contact_extensions` providing the required registrant data, `privacy_mode` controlling WHOIS redaction, and `auto_renew` opting into automatic renewal billing.
cloudflare_registrar_api_sandbox_registr: A domain registration through Cloudflare Registrar's sandbox environment -- the same real shape as cloudflare_registrar_api_registration_response_single, used for testing registration flows without a live registry transaction.
cloudflare_relay: A relay for Media over QUIC (MoQ) -- a named Cloudflare-managed relay endpoint used to publish and subscribe to MoQ media streams.
cloudflare_repo: A repository in Cloudflare's Artifacts (container registry) service. The same real entity and endpoint as cloudflare_commit (see that entry's own intro for the real noun-derivation mismatch there) -- `default_branch`/`read_only` describe the repository itself, not an individual commit.
cloudflare_request: Represents a query for Cloudforce One requests -- a paginated, filterable/sortable listing of requests by status and creation/completion time range, rather than a standalone request entity in its own right.
cloudflare_resource_group: A resource group for account-level IAM. Defines a `scope` (a set of scope objects narrowing which real account resources it covers), referenced by IAM role bindings to grant permissions over that specific resource subset instead of the whole account.
cloudflare_resource_sharing_share_exclud: An excluded recipient on a Resource Sharing share -- when a share targets a whole organization, explicitly excludes one account (`account_id`) from receiving it.
cloudflare_resource_sharing_share_recipi: A recipient on a Resource Sharing share -- grants a specific account (`recipient_account_id`) access to the resources included in the parent share.
cloudflare_resource_sharing_share_resour: A resource included in a Resource Sharing share -- references one account-owned resource (`resource_id`, `resource_type`) made available to the share's own recipients.
cloudflare_resource_sharing_share_respon: A Resource Sharing share -- the top-level container that groups a set of `resources` and grants access to a set of `recipients` (individual accounts or, via an exclusion list, a whole organization).
cloudflare_route: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway and its sibling generated names (see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list). A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_rule: A DEX (Digital Experience Monitoring) rule -- matches traffic via a wirefilter `match` expression, used to scope which traffic DEX tests and monitoring apply to.
cloudflare_rum_site_response_single: A Real User Monitoring (RUM) site. Configures the hostname RUM's own JavaScript beacon reports under, with `auto_install` controlling whether Cloudflare automatically injects the beacon for orange-clouded (proxied) sites.
cloudflare_scan: A URL scan job in Cloudflare's URL Scanner -- submits `url` for automated analysis (with optional custom headers and geo-egress `country`), returning screenshots and scan results once complete. `visibility` controls whether the scan appears in public listings.
cloudflare_secondary_dns_single_response: A Secondary DNS TSIG key -- authenticates zone transfers between Cloudflare and a primary/secondary nameserver pair using the given `algo` and shared `secret`.
A Secondary DNS peer -- a named remote nameserver Cloudflare performs zone transfers with, referenced by Secondary DNS zone configuration.
A Secondary DNS ACL -- an allowed IP range for primary/secondary nameservers performing zone transfers with Cloudflare's Secondary DNS, applied account-wide.
cloudflare_secrets_store_secret_response: The result of duplicating a Secrets Store secret -- creates a new secret (`name`, `comment`, `scopes`) as a copy of an existing one, scoped to the services listed in `scopes`.
cloudflare_secrets_store_store_response: A Secrets Store -- a named, account-level container for secrets, scoped by which Cloudflare services can read from it.
cloudflare_sensitivity_group: A DLP sensitivity group -- a named collection of sensitivity levels (`levels`), either explicit or seeded from a built-in `template_id`, that DLP profiles reference to weight how matches within the group should be treated.
cloudflare_server: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server registered with Access's AI Controls. Configures how Access connects to the upstream MCP endpoint (`hostname`, `auth_type`, `auth_credentials`), optionally routing outbound traffic through Zero Trust Secure Web Gateway.
cloudflare_sink: A sink for a Cloudflare Pipeline -- the destination an ETL pipeline writes processed events to (currently R2, per `config`), with `format`/`schema` describing the shape of the written data.
cloudflare_smartshield_single_hc_respons: A Smart Shield health check -- the same real health-check concept as cloudflare_healthchecks_single_response, scoped to Cloudflare's Smart Shield product rather than the general zone health-checks endpoint.
cloudflare_stream: A stream for a Cloudflare Pipeline -- an HTTP ingestion endpoint (`http`) or Worker binding (`worker_binding`) events are pushed into before the pipeline's own SQL processing and sink delivery.
cloudflare_stream_language_response_sing: A caption/subtitle track for a Cloudflare Stream video, in a specific `language` -- uploaded as a WebVTT file.
cloudflare_stream_live_input_response_si: A live input for Cloudflare Stream -- an ingest endpoint for a live broadcast. Configures recording behavior (`recording`, `delete_recording_after_days`) and low-latency delivery (`prefer_low_latency`) for the resulting stream.
cloudflare_stream_video_response_single: A Cloudflare Stream video, created by copying from an external `url`/`input`. Configures access control (`require_signed_urls`, `allowed_origins`), an optional `scheduled_deletion` time, and thumbnail generation.
cloudflare_stream_watermark_response_sin: A watermark profile for Cloudflare Stream -- a reusable overlay image (`url`) with configurable position, scale, opacity, and padding, applied to videos that reference the profile.
cloudflare_subscription: An event subscription in Cloudflare's Event Notifications platform. Routes matching `events` from a `source` configuration to a `destination`, the mechanism behind Cloudflare's own webhook/queue-based event delivery for account activity.
cloudflare_suppression: An email suppression entry for Email Routing -- an `email` address (with an optional `expires_at`) Cloudflare stops delivering routed mail to, typically added after a hard bounce.
cloudflare_takedown_notice: A takedown notice in Cloudforce One's Brand Protection service -- tracks the lifecycle (`status`) of a takedown request against an infringing `domain`, linked to the `match_id`/`match_type` that triggered it and the letters (see cloudflare_letter) sent as part of the process.
cloudflare_target: An infrastructure target for Cloudflare's Infrastructure Access product -- a non-unique `hostname` and `ip` pair identifying a real machine or service that Zero Trust access policies can target for SSH/RDP-style access.
cloudflare_target_environment: A target environment for Vulnerability Scanner -- identifies a Cloudflare asset (currently zone-typed only, via `target`'s own discriminator) the scanner is authorized to scan.
cloudflare_teams_devices_components_sche: A device managed network for Zero Trust -- defines how the WARP client detects it's on a specific trusted network (`config`, `type`), used to apply network-aware device policies.
cloudflare_teams_devices_device_settings: A WARP client device settings policy -- account-wide (or matched-device) configuration for WARP client behavior: mode switching, auto-connect/reconnect timing, captive portal handling, DNS search suffixes, and tunnel route inclusion/exclusion.
cloudflare_teams_devices_schemas_single_: A device posture integration for Zero Trust -- connects a third-party posture-check API (`type`, `config`) that WARP client posture rules can reference, polled on the given `interval`.
cloudflare_teams_devices_single_response: A device posture rule for Zero Trust -- a named check (`type`, `match`, `input`) evaluated against a device on a polling `schedule`, whose pass/fail result feeds Access policies' own device-posture conditions.
cloudflare_template: A letter template in Cloudforce One's Brand Protection service -- reusable takedown-notice text (`body`, `category`, `source`) that takedown notice letters are generated from.
cloudflare_tls_certificates_and_hostname: A custom SSL/TLS certificate uploaded to a zone -- `certificate`/`private_key` (or a reference to an already-submitted CSR via `custom_csr_id`), with `geo_restrictions`/`policy` controlling where the private key may be held.
A Cloudflare Origin CA certificate -- issued by Cloudflare's own origin certificate authority for the `hostnames` listed, from a submitted `csr`, valid for `requested_validity` days.
The zone-level Authenticated Origin Pulls certificate -- the client certificate Cloudflare presents to the zone's own origin server to authenticate edge-to-origin requests.

A per-hostname Authenticated Origin Pulls certificate -- the same real mechanism as cloudflare_tls_certificates_and_hostnames_certificate_response_single_3, scoped to an individual custom hostname rather than the whole zone.

An account-level mTLS certificate -- a CA or leaf certificate (`ca` discriminates which) usable across the account wherever mutual TLS is needed, including as a custom certificate for Zero Trust's own block page.
A zone-level client (mTLS) certificate -- issued from a submitted `csr`, valid for `validity_days`, used to authenticate client devices connecting to the zone.

A zone-level Certificate Signing Request (CSR) generated by Cloudflare -- `common_name`/`sans`/organization fields describe the certificate to be signed; the resulting CSR can be submitted to an external CA or used with `custom_csr_id` on a custom certificate upload.
An account-level Certificate Signing Request (CSR), the same real concept as cloudflare_tls_certificates_and_hostnames_custom_csr_response_single scoped to the account rather than a single zone.

A custom hostname for SSL for SaaS -- a customer-owned hostname (`hostname`) CNAMEd to the zone, with `ssl` controlling its own certificate provisioning and `custom_origin_server`/`custom_origin_sni` optionally routing it to a different origin than the zone's own default.
A zone-level custom trust store entry -- a root CA certificate Cloudflare trusts when validating a client or origin connection, beyond the public CAs trusted by default.

A Keyless SSL certificate configuration -- lets Cloudflare terminate TLS for `host` while the private key stays on the customer's own Keyless SSL server (reached at `host`:`port`, optionally through a Cloudflare Tunnel), rather than uploading the key to Cloudflare.

A per-hostname TLS setting override -- sets a specific TLS setting (`setting_id`, e.g. allowed cipher suites) for a single `hostname` within the zone, distinct from the zone's own default TLS configuration.
cloudflare_token: An API token for AI Search -- credentials (`cf_api_id`/`cf_api_key`) an AI Search instance uses to call other Cloudflare APIs on the account's behalf.
cloudflare_tree: A repository in Cloudflare's Artifacts (container registry) service -- the same real entity and endpoint as cloudflare_commit and cloudflare_repo (see cloudflare_commit's own intro for the real noun-derivation mismatch shared by all three).
cloudflare_trigger: A Cron Trigger binding for a Worker script (`script_name`) -- schedules the named Worker to run on a cron schedule, configured via this endpoint's own request body rather than a separately-named field set (the response envelope carries no real trigger-specific fields beyond the generic success wrapper).
cloudflare_tunnel_cfd_tunnel_response_si: A Cloudflare Tunnel -- a persistent, outbound-only connection from an origin to Cloudflare's network. `config_src` distinguishes a locally-YAML-configured tunnel from one whose configuration is managed remotely via the API/dashboard.
cloudflare_tunnel_hostname_route_respons: A hostname route for Cloudflare Tunnel (Zero Trust networking) -- directs traffic for a specific `hostname` to the tunnel identified by `tunnel_id`.
cloudflare_tunnel_route_response_single: A network route for Cloudflare Tunnel -- directs traffic for a private IP `network` (CIDR) to the tunnel identified by `tunnel_id`, optionally scoped to a specific `virtual_network_id`.
cloudflare_tunnel_subnet_response_single: A WARP subnet for Zero Trust networking -- a private IP range (`network`) WARP-connected devices can reach, with `is_default_network` marking the account's own single default subnet.
cloudflare_tunnel_vnet_response_single: A virtual network for Cloudflare Tunnel -- an isolated routing namespace tunnel routes can be scoped to, letting the same private IP ranges be reused across separate virtual networks without conflict. `is_default`/`is_default_network` mark the account's own default.
cloudflare_tunnel_warp_connector_respons: A WARP Connector -- a Cloudflare Tunnel variant purpose-built to connect a private network to Cloudflare's Zero Trust WARP overlay, with `ha` opting into a highly-available multi-connector setup.
cloudflare_url: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway and its sibling generated names (see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list). A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_url_ignore_pattern: A URL ignore pattern for Email Security -- a regular expression (`pattern`) identifying URLs that should be exempt from Email Security's own link-rewriting/scanning behavior.
cloudflare_user_group: A User group for account-level IAM -- a named collection of IAM `policies` assigned as a unit to users, instead of attaching policies to each user individually.
cloudflare_user_schema: A user-uploaded API schema for API Shield's schema validation feature -- the same real concept as cloudflare_api_shield_public_schema_success_result, discovered via a distinct read path that emphasizes the schema's own `file`-upload creation flow.
cloudflare_version: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway and its sibling generated names (see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list). A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_waf_product_api_bundle_respon: A custom leaked-credential-check detection for the WAF -- a zone-level rule matching `username`/`password` fields in request bodies against ruleset expressions, extending Cloudflare's own built-in leaked-credential detections with account-specific ones.
cloudflare_waitingroom_event_response: A scheduled event for a Waiting Room -- temporarily overrides the parent waiting room's own settings (queueing method, session duration, custom page, new-user admission rate) for the duration between `event_start_time` and `event_end_time`, reverting to the room's own defaults for any field left null.
cloudflare_waitingroom_single_response: A Waiting Room for a zone -- queues visitors to `host` (and optionally specific paths, via `additional_routes` on Advanced plans) when origin capacity is constrained, controlling queue behavior, cookie handling, and the rendered waiting page.
cloudflare_web3_content_list_entry_singl: A content list entry for a Web3/IPFS gateway hostname -- blocks a specific IPFS `content` (CID or content path) of the given `type` from being served through the gateway.
cloudflare_web3_single_response: A Web3 hostname -- a zone hostname that gateways requests to a decentralized `target` (e.g. IPFS, via `dnslink`), letting a normal DNS-resolvable hostname serve content from a Web3 network.
cloudflare_widget: A Turnstile widget -- Cloudflare's CAPTCHA alternative. Configures challenge behavior (`mode`, `bot_fight_mode`), which `domains` it's valid on, branding (`offlabel`), and the availability `region`, identified by its own `sitekey`.
cloudflare_worker: A Workers Build configuration -- connects a Worker to a `git_repository` for CI-driven deployment, with `production_settings` controlling the build/deploy behavior for production pushes.
cloudflare_workers_namespace_single_resp: A Workers for Platforms dispatch namespace -- an isolated deployment target multiple customer Workers ('user Workers') can be deployed into, then dynamically dispatched to from a single entrypoint Worker.
cloudflare_workers_versions_single_respo: A version of a Worker script (`script_name`) -- an uploaded, immutable snapshot of the script's own `files`/`metadata` at a point in time, referenced by `version_id`. A script's own gradual/canary deployments select traffic percentages across versions rather than replacing the live script outright.
cloudflare_workflow: A Cloudflare Workflow -- a durable-execution definition (`class_name` naming the Worker class implementing it, `script_name` the owning Worker) with configurable `concurrency`, `limits`, `schedules`, and `default_retention` for its own run instances.
cloudflare_zero_trust_gateway_list_singl: A Gateway list -- a named, reusable collection of `items` (e.g. domains, IPs) Zero Trust Gateway policies reference by list instead of enumerating values inline.
cloudflare_zero_trust_gateway_single_res: A Gateway certificate -- the TLS certificate Zero Trust Gateway uses for TLS decryption/inspection, with `validity_period_days` controlling the certificate's own lifetime.

A Gateway location -- a named network location (identified by its own `networks`/CIDR ranges) DNS/HTTP/network policies can be scoped to, with `client_default` marking the account's own default location and `dns_destination_ips_id` binding it to a specific pair of resolver IPs.

A Gateway rule -- the core policy unit of Zero Trust Secure Web Gateway. Matches traffic via `filters`/`identity`/`device_posture` wirefilter expressions and applies `action` when matched, evaluated across rules in ascending `precedence` order.

A Gateway proxy endpoint -- a dedicated IP/port Zero Trust Gateway exposes for a specific proxy `kind`, used when traffic needs to reach Gateway through a fixed, dedicated address rather than the shared WARP/PAC-file path.

A Gateway PAC file -- a hosted Proxy Auto-Configuration file (`contents`) devices can be pointed at to route traffic through Zero Trust Gateway without the WARP client, addressable at a URL-friendly `slug`.
cloudflare_zone: A Cloudflare zone -- the core unit of the platform, representing a domain (`name`) onboarded to Cloudflare. `type` distinguishes a full zone (DNS hosted with Cloudflare) from a partial zone (partner-hosted DNS, Cloudflare added via CNAME).
